newsitem.title: CHINA: China condemns three to die for riots - report.
newsitem.headline: China condemns three to die for riots - report.

text.p: China has sentenced three people to death and 27 to prison for their role in bloody riots in the Moslem region of Xinjiang in February, local television said in a report monitored by the BBC on Saturday.

The three men were condemned to death in a public rally on Thursday for the crimes of malicious wounding, arson and hooliganism during riots in Yining near the Kazakh border that killed at least nine people and injured 198, the report said.
Local officials were not immediately available for comment.
One man was condemned to life in prison for hooliganism and the other 26 were given jail terms ranging from seven to 18 years, the report said.

The television report quoted a local Communist Party official as saying at the rally that a "handful of serious criminal offenders" had "burnt vehicles and houses and killed public security policemen and innocent people".
"What they did... seriously disturbed and disrupted our political stability and unity," the official was quoted as saying.
The report did not say if those sentenced were of the ethnic Uighur minority that make up a large part of Xinjiang's population.
Xinjiang, a vast region that is home to many Turkic-speaking peoples like the Uighurs, has a long history of ethnic friction and has recently been rocked by Moslem separatist violence.
Uighur militants say they want to set up their own state of "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang.
Xinjiang's capital of Urumqi was rocked by a series of bus bombs last month in attacks that killed nine and wounded 74.
Uighur exiles have claimed responsibility for the bombings and vowed to stage more attacks until they gain freedom for their homeland.
Officials said last month they had ended hearings for six men on trial for their part in anti-Chinese rioting that began as a demonstration for Xinjiang independence and turned violent.
